transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well, doctor, I came in because at church I’ve been doing some odd things. Like I’ll stand by the potluck table holding up the serving spoon and just not move. Or I’ll fold the same stack of napkins over and over while folks are waiting on me. It’s embarrassing, and I don’t quite know why I’m doing it.
When you keep folding the napkins over and over, does it feel like you have to do it to relieve a strong inner urge or anxiety?

I don’t know that it’s to calm me down, exactly. It’s more that I just get stuck doing it. I’ll be there at church folding the same napkins again and again, or standing there with the serving spoon held up, and people are waiting on me. It feels odd, but I can’t quite explain why I’m doing it.
When you get stuck like that, do people have a hard time getting your attention?

Yes, sometimes. I’ll be standing there with that serving spoon raised, or folding the napkins over and over, and folks have to kind of call to me or wait on me. I don’t mean to ignore them—I just get stuck in it for a bit.
Do you ever hear voices when no one else is there?
No, I don’t think so. I haven’t noticed hearing voices when nobody’s there.
Have there been times when you felt unusually full of energy and needed much less sleep than usual?
No, I don’t think I’ve had that. I sleep about the same as usual, far as I can tell. I haven’t felt full of energy like that.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most days?
I’m not sure I’d call it depressed. I have my quiet days, but I haven’t really noticed feeling down most days.
Since you were a child, have you usually found it hard to understand social cues or make back-and-forth conversation?

I don’t really know. I don’t think I had a big problem with that as a child, not that I remember. I was quiet sometimes, but I can’t say I noticed trouble understanding people or talking back and forth.
Before these episodes started, had you been diagnosed with any new medical or neurological illness?
No, not that I know of. I don’t remember being told I had any new medical or nerve problem before that.
Do you have a strong belief that other people would say is not true or doesn’t make sense?
I don’t think so. I mean, I have my own thoughts about things, but I can’t say there’s some strong belief that people keep telling me is wrong or doesn’t make sense.
Have you started using any new drugs or medications recently?
No, I don’t think so. I haven’t started any new drugs or medicines recently, not that I can remember.
Have you had any seizures?
No, I don’t think I’ve had any seizures. Not that I’m aware of.
Have people told you that your speech has become hard to follow or jumbled?

Yes… some people have said that. Like when the ladies ask me about blankets or choir practice, I try to answer plain, but my words get away from me. I’ll start talking about beans, then hymns, then my roses, and they look at me like they can’t follow what I’m saying.
Have you been told by a doctor that you have any brain illness or other medical condition that could affect how you move or think?
No, I don’t think any doctor has told me I have a brain illness or anything like that. I’m not sure what all would count, but I haven’t been told that.
Do you ever feel like an outside force is controlling your thoughts or movements?
I don’t think so. I mean, sometimes I get mixed up in my own head, but I haven’t felt like somebody else is making me move or putting thoughts in there.
Have people told you that your face often looks blank or that you show very little emotion?
I don’t know… I haven’t really noticed that. I don’t think anyone’s told me my face looks blank. Maybe I’m quiet sometimes, but I’m not sure what they see.
Have you had any fevers around the times these episodes happen?
I don’t think so. I haven’t noticed having a fever when those things happen.
Do your thoughts ever feel jumbled or hard to keep in order?

Yes… sometimes they do. Like when the ladies ask me something simple, about blankets or choir practice, I mean to answer plain, but then my words kind of wander. I start on one thing and end up talking about beans, or hymns, or my roses. Then people look at me like they can’t follow what I’m saying.
Have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy?
I’m not really sure. I still like some of the things I used to, I think. Maybe I don’t do them as much, but I wouldn’t say I’ve lost interest.
Have any doctors ever said these episodes are caused by a medical problem in your body or brain?
No, not that I know of. I don’t remember any doctor saying it was from something wrong in my body or my brain.
Have any doctors ever told you that these episodes are caused by a medical illness?
I don’t think so. I don’t remember any doctor telling me it was from a medical illness.
